mainTopic: The greatness of ירושלים of the future, and how far a ship must be pulled to acquire it
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier אגדה, where ה׳ says He decreed death on אדם הראשון. The גמרא then brings a series of teachings about ירושלים of the future. Only invited people will go up to it. The צדיקים, משיח, and ירושלים will be called by ה׳'s name, and "קדוש" will be said before the צדיקים. ירושלים will be raised three פרסאות high, and people will fly up to it like clouds and doves. The angels protest a plan to give it a fixed size, so it will spread out without walls, with huge additions each as big as צפורי and buildings many floors high. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and brings a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל on how far a ship must be pulled to acquire it. A first attempt to match their views to a ברייתא about animals fails, and a second attempt with a ברייתא about ships continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line: death decreed on the first man
steps.stepSummary: The last words of an earlier אגדה, in which ה׳ says He decreed death on אדם הראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I decreed death on אדם הראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a story that started before this section, where ה׳ is speaking. It closes that topic so the גמרא can move on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement itself began earlier on the דף, so this line is only its ending. Here ה׳ says He made people mortal by decreeing death on אדם הראשון. The next line starts a new topic.

phrases.english: And I decreed death on Adam, the first man.
phrases.notes: This is ה׳ speaking, finishing a statement that started earlier on the דף.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָנַסְתִּי מִיתָה עַל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends an אגדה that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ה׳ decreed death on אדם הראשון.

steps.title: What does 'those invited to it' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the פסוק about Mount Zion and asks what the words "and over those invited to it" mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by "and over those invited to it"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of one phrase in a פסוק. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on anything. The גמרא just wants to know why the פסוק adds "those invited to it" when it has already spoken about Mount Zion itself.

phrases.english: What is meant by "and over those invited to it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְעַל מִקְרָאֶהָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining a phrase in a פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase "and over those invited to it" in ישעיהו 4:5.

steps.title: Only invited people go up to future Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן says that anyone can go up to ירושלים of this world, but only invited people can go up to ירושלים of the עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: ירושלים of the עולם הבא is not like ירושלים of this world. Anyone who wants to go up to ירושלים of this world can go up. Only those invited can go up to the ירושלים of the עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question in Step 2. "Those invited to it" are the people who are allowed to go up to the future ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן compares two cities. Today ירושלים is open to anyone who wants to go. The future ירושלים will be open only to people who are invited to it, and that is what "מקראה" in the פסוק is describing.
steps.whatToRemember: ירושלים of this world is open to all, but the future ירושלים is only for those invited to it.

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Not like Jerusalem of this world
is Jerusalem of the World-to-Come.
Jerusalem of this world:
anyone who wants to go up, goes up.
That of the World-to-Come:
none go up except those invited to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא כִּירוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Those invited to it" are the only people who may go up to ירושלים of the עולם הבא, unlike today's ירושלים, which anyone may go up to.

steps.title: The righteous will be called by ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching from רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן: in the future, צדיקים will be called by the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא, and a פסוק in ישעיהו is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה also said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In the future, the צדיקים will be called by the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: "Everyone who is called by My name, and whom I created for My glory, I formed him, I even made him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same speakers. It says the צדיקים will one day carry ה׳'s name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the פסוק "everyone who is called by My name... whom I created for My glory." רבי יוחנן reads it as describing the צדיקים, who bring glory to ה׳ and so will be called by His name.

keyTerms.meaning: who are called by His name
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: And Rabba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
In the future, the righteous will be called

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is said: "Everyone who is called by My name,
and whom I created for My glory,
I formed him, I even made him."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עֲתִידִין צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same speakers, connected by the phrase "ואמר."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, צדיקים will be called by the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא (ישעיהו 43:7).

steps.title: Three things called by ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יוחנן lists three things called by ה׳'s name: צדיקים, משיח, and ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Three are called by the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא, and they are the צדיקים, משיח, and ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second student of רבי יוחנן widens the idea from Step 4. It is not only the צדיקים who carry ה׳'s name; there is a list of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 spoke only about the צדיקים. This teaching adds משיח and ירושלים. The list does not give sources, so the גמרא will supply them in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Three are called by the name
of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and these are they: the righteous, the Messiah, and Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה נִקְרְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds משיח and ירושלים to the צדיקים mentioned in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three are called by ה׳'s name: צדיקים, משיח, and ירושלים.

steps.title: Sources for each of the three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a source for each item on the list. For צדיקים it uses the פסוק already quoted, for משיח a פסוק in ירמיהו, and for ירושלים a פסוק in יחזקאל read with an אל תקרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the צדיקים, the source is what we already said. For משיח, it is written: "And this is his name by which he will be called: ה׳ is our righteousness." For ירושלים, it is written: "It shall be eighteen thousand all around, and the name of the city from that day: ה׳ is there (שָׁמָּה)." Do not read "שָׁמָּה" (there), but "שְׁמָהּ" (its name).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up each part of רבי יוחנן's list with a פסוק. For ירושלים it changes how one word is read to make the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדיקים are covered by the פסוק from Step 4. For משיח, the פסוק says his name will be "ה׳ is our righteousness." For ירושלים, the word "שָׁמָּה" (there) is read as "שְׁמָהּ" (its name), so the city's name becomes "ה׳."

keyTerms.meaning: this is what we already said
do not read (it this way), but rather...

steps.confusionAlert: "אל תקרי" does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong. The letters stay the same; the גמרא reads them with different vowels to draw out an extra lesson.
steps.whatToRemember: צדיקים (ישעיהו 43:7), משיח (ירמיהו 23:6), and ירושלים (יחזקאל 48:35) are all called by ה׳'s name.

phrases.english: The righteous: this is what we said.
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק from ישעיהו quoted just before.

phrases.english: The Messiah: as it is written:
"And this is his name by which he shall be called:
the Lord is our righteousness."
Jerusalem: as it is written:
"It shall be eighteen thousand all around,
and the name of the city from that day: the Lord is there."
Do not read "there" (shamma),
but rather "its name" (shemah).

steps.triggerLanguage: צַדִּיקִים – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק for each of the three items listed in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That צדיקים, משיח, and ירושלים are each called by ה׳'s name.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 43:7 (צדיקים), ירמיהו 23:6 (משיח), and יחזקאל 48:35 read as "שמה" (its name) (ירושלים).

steps.title: "Holy" will be said before the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that in the future people will say "קדוש" before the צדיקים, the way it is said before הקדוש ברוך הוא, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: In the future, people will say "קדוש" before the צדיקים, the way they say it before הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: "And whoever is left in Zion and whoever remains in ירושלים will be called holy."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher adds another way the צדיקים will be honored in the future. People will call them "holy."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4 to 6 were about being called by ה׳'s name. רבי אלעזר adds that the word "קדוש," which we say about ה׳, will also be said about the צדיקים. His proof is the פסוק "קדוש יאמר לו," "holy will be said of him."
steps.whatToRemember: In the future, the צדיקים will be called by ה׳'s name, and "קדוש" will be said before them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
In the future, the righteous will have "Holy" said before them,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: the way it is said before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is said: "And whoever is left in Zion
and whoever remains in Jerusalem
will be called holy."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: עֲתִידִין צַדִּיקִים שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לִפְנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another future honor for the צדיקים, alongside being called by ה׳'s name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, people will say "קדוש" before the צדיקים, as they do before ה׳‎ (ישעיהו 4:3).

steps.title: ירושלים will be raised three פרסאות high
steps.stepSummary: רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן teaches that in the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will lift ירושלים three פרסאות upward. He reads the word תחתיה in a פסוק in זכריה as 'matching its size.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In the future, ה׳ will raise ירושלים three פרסאות upward, as the פסוק says, 'And it shall be lifted up and settled in its place.' What does 'in its place' mean? It means 'like its place': the height will match the size of the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן about ירושלים of the future: it will be lifted three פרסאות into the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the word תחתיה. It is read as כתחתיה, 'equal to its place,' meaning the height ירושלים rises equals the size of its area. This sets up the next question: how do we know the area was three פרסאות?

keyTerms.meaning: A long distance measure, roughly a few kilometers (plural: פַּרְסָאוֹת)
'In its place'; here read as 'matching its size'
Like its place, equal to its own measure

phrases.english: And Rabba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will raise Jerusalem
three parasangs upward,
as it is stated: "And it shall be lifted up and settled in its place";
What is "in its place"? Like its place.
phrases.notes: He means the city will rise as high as its own size, so its area gives the height.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבה in the name of רבי יוחנן about the future ירושלים, continuing the series from Steps 3-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future ירושלים will be raised three פרסאות, learned from תחתיה read as כתחתיה.

steps.title: How do we know the city's size was three פרסאות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the number three comes from, since the פסוק only says the height matches the city's size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this 'place' of ירושלים was three פרסאות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to fill a gap in the last teaching, and the next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says the height will equal the city's size. To get 'three פרסאות' we still need to know how big ירושלים actually was.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this "place"
was three parasangs?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּהַאי תַּחְתֶּיהָ תְּלָתָא פַּרְסֵי הָוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the missing fact behind the number in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original size of ירושלים, which sets the height it will be raised.

steps.title: An old man saw that the first ירושלים was three פרסאות
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports that an old man told him he had seen the first ירושלים, and it was three פרסאות in size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: A certain old man told me, 'I myself saw the first ירושלים, and it was three פרסאות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question with eyewitness testimony from an old man who saw ירושלים before it was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is not from a פסוק but from someone who saw it. Since the first ירושלים measured three פרסאות, the future city will be raised three פרסאות.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
A certain old man said to me:
I myself saw the first Jerusalem,
and it was three parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אֲמַר לִי הָהוּא סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An eyewitness saw that the first ירושלים was three פרסאות, so that is the measure.

steps.title: Wouldn't climbing so high be hard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a worry: if ירושלים is three פרסאות up in the air, going up there would be painful and difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps you will say: there will be hardship in going up there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible problem with the raised ירושלים, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A city that high sounds hard to reach. That would seem to make the future ירושלים worse, not better, so the גמרא must show there is no such difficulty.

phrases.english: And perhaps you will say:
There is hardship in going up?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר יֵשׁ צַעַר לַעֲלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a practical difficulty with the teaching of Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that ירושלים will be raised three פרסאות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a height would make it painful to go up to ירושלים.

steps.title: People will fly up like clouds and doves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from a פסוק in ישעיהו: the people will fly to ירושלים like clouds and doves, so there is no hardship.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'Who are these that fly like a cloud, and like doves to their windows?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry with a פסוק showing that people will fly up to ירושלים easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes people flying like a cloud and like doves heading home. Flying takes no effort, so the height of ירושלים causes no hardship.

keyTerms.meaning: Windows or openings, here the doves' nesting holes

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Who are these that fly like a cloud,
and like doves to their windows?"

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר מִי אֵלֶּה כָּעָב תְּעוּפֶינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural proof that removes the difficulty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going up to a raised ירושלים would be hard.
steps.terutzMaskana: People will fly there easily like clouds and doves.

steps.title: רב פפא learns that clouds are three פרסאות high
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws a side fact from the last teaching: clouds rise three פרסאות high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that this cloud rises three פרסאות high.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a side point that follows from putting the last two steps together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושלים will be three פרסאות high, and people will reach it 'like a cloud.' So a cloud must be able to reach three פרסאות high.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Learn from this
that this cloud rises three parasangs high.
phrases.notes: People fly 'like a cloud' up to a ירושלים three פרסאות high, so clouds must go that high too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side inference by combining Step 8 and Step 12.

steps.title: ה׳ wanted to give ירושלים a set size
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to give ירושלים fixed measurements. He brings the vision in זכריה of a man going to measure the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: ה׳ wanted to give ירושלים a set measurement, as it says: 'And I said, Where are you going? And he said to me: To measure ירושלים, to see how wide it is and how long it is.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: at first, הקדוש ברוך הוא planned to give ירושלים a fixed size. This sets up the angels' protest in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is זכריה's vision of a man with a measuring line going to measure ירושלים's width and length. That shows there was a plan to fix the city's borders.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to give Jerusalem a set measurement,
as it is stated: "And I said: Where are you going?
And he said to me: To measure Jerusalem,
to see how much is its width and how much is its length" –

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא בִּקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לָתֵת אֶת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם בְּמִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about ירושלים of the future, from a different אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא first planned to give ירושלים fixed measurements.

steps.title: The angels protest giving ירושלים a limit
steps.stepSummary: The מלאכי השרת argue: the cities of the nations have no fixed size, so how can ירושלים, holy as it is, be limited?
steps.simpleTranslation: The מלאכי השרת said before ה׳: רבונו של עולם, You created many big cities in Your world for the nations, and You did not give them a measure of length and width. ירושלים, which has Your name in it, Your מקדש in it, and צדיקים in it, You will give it a measure?!
steps.whatsHappening: The angels challenge the plan to put a fixed size on ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their argument compares the two: cities of the nations can grow without limit. ירושלים is far more important because of ה׳'s name, the מקדש, and the צדיקים in it, so it should not get less than they do.

phrases.english: The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
You created many large cities
in Your world for the nations of the world,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נָתַתָּ מִדַּת אׇרְכָּן וּמִדַּת רׇחְבָּן;
phrases.english: and You did not give a measure of their length or a measure of their width;
Jerusalem, which has Your name in it,
and Your Temple in it, and righteous people in it –
You are giving it a measure?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plan described in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan to give ירושלים a fixed measurement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cities of the nations have no limits, so it makes no sense for the holy city ירושלים to be limited.

steps.title: ירושלים will spread out without walls
steps.stepSummary: Right away the message came in זכריה's prophecy: ירושלים will be settled like open towns without walls, because of how many people and animals will fill it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: 'And he said to him: Run, speak to this young man, saying: ירושלים will be settled like open towns without walls, because of the many people and animals in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the angels' protest is accepted, and the פסוק announces that ירושלים will have no fixed borders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיד shows the plan changed right away. פרזות means open towns without walls, so ירושלים will keep growing to hold its huge population and will have no set size.
steps.whatToRemember: ירושלים of the future will be raised three פרסאות high, people will fly up to it easily, and it will have no fixed borders because so many people will fill it.

phrases.english: Immediately:
"And he said to him: Run, speak
to this young man, saying:
Jerusalem will be settled like open towns without walls,
because of the many people and animals in it."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָו רֻץ דַּבֵּר אֶל הַנַּעַר הַלָּז לֵאמֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the angels' protest in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ירושלים will not be given a fixed measure; it will spread out without walls because of its many inhabitants.

steps.title: ריש לקיש on the huge future additions to Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that in the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will add thousands of gardens, towers, fortresses and small houses to ירושלים, each the size of צפורי at its height.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will add to ירושלים a thousand times 'טפף' of gardens, a thousand times 'כפל' of towers, a thousand times 'ליצוי' of fortresses, and a thousand and two times 'שילה' of small houses. Each one of these will be as big as צפורי was in its best days.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש adds another teaching about how huge ירושלים will become in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each odd word (טפף, כפל, ליצוי, שילה) stands for a number by adding up the values of its letters. So the additions are thousands times those numbers, and each single addition is as big as the great city of צפורי. This continues the theme of the last step: ירושלים will have no fixed limit.

keyTerms.meaning: the city of צפורי in its prosperity

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
In the future, the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will add to Jerusalem
one thousand times 'tefaf' of gardens,
phrases.notes: Each odd word here is a number made by adding its letters. For example, טפף is 9+80+80, which is 169.

phrases.english: one thousand times 'kefel' of towers,
one thousand times 'litzoy' of fortresses,
one thousand and two times 'shilo' of small houses;
and each and every one
will be like Tzippori in its prosperity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהוֹסִיף עַל יְרוּשְׁלֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the idea that ירושלים will have no fixed size.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Future ירושלים will gain thousands of gardens, towers, fortresses and houses, each the size of צפורי at its height.

steps.title: How big צפורי was at its height
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי: he saw צפורי at its height, and it had 180,000 markets just of sellers of pot sauces.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said: I saw צפורי in its prosperity, and it had one hundred and eighty thousand markets of people selling pot sauces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show how big צפורי was, so we can picture the comparison ריש לקיש just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש compared each addition to צפורי, but we need to know how big צפורי was. רבי יוסי, who saw it himself, says it had 180,000 markets for just one kind of food. That shows how vast each future addition to ירושלים will be.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
I saw Tzippori in its prosperity,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ בָּהּ מֵאָה וּשְׁמוֹנִים אֶלֶף שְׁוָוקִים
phrases.english: and there were in it one hundred and eighty thousand markets
of sellers of pot sauces.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי צִפּוֹרִי בְּשַׁלְווֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the comparison to צפורי in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צפורי at its height had 180,000 markets of sauce sellers.

steps.title: What does 'thirty-three times' in יחזקאל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל about side-chambers 'three and thirty times' and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the side-chambers were one over another, three and thirty times.' What does 'three and thirty times' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק and asks what its odd number means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'three and thirty times' is strange. The גמרא wants to know what it is describing, and the answer will tie it to the future size of ירושלים.

phrases.english: "And the side-chambers were one over another,
three and thirty times" —
What is "three and thirty times"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״שָׁלוֹשׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁים פְּעָמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new פסוק on the same theme of future ירושלים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'three and thirty times' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Three times wider with thirty floors, or thirty times wider with three floors
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי, in the name of רב פפי from רבי יהושע דסכני, explains: if ירושלים grows three times, each house will be thirty floors high; if it grows thirty times, each will be three floors high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said that רב פפי said in the name of רבי יהושע דסכני: If ירושלים becomes three times its size, each house will have thirty floors above it. If ירושלים becomes thirty times its size, each house will have three floors above it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the numbers three and thirty describe how ירושלים will grow, in width and in height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'three' and 'thirty' are split between how wide the city gets and how tall the buildings are. Either way, the total growth is the same. It fits the idea that future ירושלים will hold huge numbers of people.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches one big message: future ירושלים will be enormous, both wider and taller.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּסִכְנִי:
phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnei:
If they are three Jerusalems,
phrases.notes: He means: if the city becomes three times as big as it was.

phrases.english: each and every one has in it
thirty floors upward;
if they are thirty Jerusalems,
each and every one has in it
three floors upward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי, אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּסִכְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three and thirty means either three times the area with thirty floors, or thirty times the area with three floors.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue how much a ship must be pulled to acquire it
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה about selling a ship: רב says pulling it any amount acquires it; שמואל says the buyer acquires only after pulling the whole ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A ship. רב said: once the buyer pulls it even a little, he acquires it. שמואל said: he does not acquire it until he pulls the whole ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה is over, and the גמרא returns to the משנה about selling a ship, bringing a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ship is acquired by משיכה (pulling it). The question is how far. רב says any small movement is enough; שמואל says the buyer must pull the entire ship its full length.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated (a dispute of אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this step continues the story about ירושלים. The topic changes completely back to the משנה about buying a ship.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new halachic discussion about how big objects are acquired by pulling.

phrases.english: It was stated: A ship —
phrases.notes: This goes back to our משנה, which talks about selling a ship.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁמָּשַׁךְ כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – קָנָה.
phrases.english: Rav said: once he pulled it any amount, he acquired it.
And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא קָנָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְשׁוֹךְ אֶת כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: He does not acquire it until he pulls the whole of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: סְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the אגדה and returns to the משנה's topic of acquiring a ship.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: pulling a ship any amount acquires it. שמואל: only pulling the whole ship acquires it.

steps.title: A ברייתא on acquiring an animal by grabbing or by pulling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the רב/שמואל dispute matches a dispute of תנאים, and quotes a ברייתא about acquiring an animal by מסירה and by משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute of תנאים. How is an animal acquired by passing? If he grabbed it by its hoof, its hair, the saddle or load on it, the bit in its mouth, or the bell on its neck, he acquired it. How is it acquired by pulling? If he calls it and it comes, or hits it with a stick and it runs in front of him, once it lifts a front leg and a back leg, he acquired it. רבי אחי (some say רבי אחא) says: not until it walks its full length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a ברייתא where תנאים argue about how far an animal must move before it is acquired, so it can compare that to רב and שמואל on the ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two ways to acquire an animal. For משיכה, the תנא קמא says one step (lifting a front leg and a back leg) is enough, while רבי אחא requires the animal to move its whole length. This looks a lot like 'a little' (רב) versus 'the whole thing' (שמואל).

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this argument is the same as an earlier argument between תנאים
Acquiring an animal by grabbing hold of it or its gear
Acquiring by pulling or making the item move toward you
The animal lifted a front leg and a back leg
Its full length, so the whole animal has moved

phrases.english: Let us say this is like a dispute of Tannaim:
How is an animal acquired through passing?
If he grabbed it by its hoof, by its hair,
by the saddle on it, by the load on it,
by the bit in its mouth, by the bell on its neck, he acquired it.
How is it acquired through pulling?
He calls it and it comes,
or he hit it with a stick and it ran in front of him,
once it lifted a front leg and a back leg, he acquired it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחַי וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Achai, and some say Rabbi Acha, says:
Not until it walks its full length.
phrases.notes: He means all four legs have moved, so the whole animal has shifted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to find an earlier tannaitic source for the רב/שמואל dispute about pulling a ship.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב and שמואל on how much of the ship must be pulled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the תנא קמא and רבי אחא argue about how far an animal must move to be acquired by משיכה.

steps.title: Matching רב and שמואל to the two sides of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the suggested match: רב follows the תנא קמא and שמואל follows רבי אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say רב holds like the תנא קמא, and שמואל holds like רבי אחא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the comparison clearly: 'a little movement is enough' goes with רב, and 'full movement is needed' goes with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this match were true, רב and שמואל would simply be repeating an older argument. The next two steps will test whether each of them really needs to depend on one side.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Shall we say Rav rules like the first Tanna
and Shmuel rules like Rabbi Acha?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב דְּאָמַר כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא just quoted to רב and שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are רב and שמואל just following the two sides of the ברייתא about animals?

steps.title: רב can fit even רבי אחא, because a ship moves all at once
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that even רבי אחא would agree with him about a ship, since a ship moves as one piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could tell you: I can hold my view even according to רבי אחא. רבי אחא only said his rule about animals, because even after lifting a front leg and a back leg, the animal is still standing in its place. But a ship: once a little of it moves, all of it moves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the match from רב's side. It shows that רב does not need to argue with רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal can lift a leg without its body really going anywhere, so רבי אחא wants full movement. A ship is one solid object, so any small movement means the whole ship moved. That is why רב says a little pulling is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his rule in this specific case
It is still standing in its place

phrases.english: Rav could say to you:
I said my ruling even according to Rabbi Acha.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha only said his rule
about animals,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּעָקְרָה יָד וָרֶגֶל –
phrases.english: because even though it lifted a front leg and a back leg,
it is still standing in its place.
But a ship,
once a little of it moves,
all of it moves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the half of the match that ties רב to the תנא קמא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב must disagree with רבי אחא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored that a ship, unlike an animal, moves entirely once part of it moves.

steps.title: שמואל can fit even the תנא קמא, because an animal's other legs are ready to follow
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that even the תנא קמא would agree with him about a ship, since a ship has no 'next step' that follows by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל could say: I can hold my view even according to the תנא קמא. The תנא קמא only said his rule about animals, because once a front leg and back leg are lifted, the other legs are ready to be lifted too. But a ship: if he pulls the whole thing, yes, he acquires it; if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the match from שמואל's side too. So neither רב nor שמואל has to be tied to one side of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an animal, one step is the start of walking, so the rest of the movement is basically on its way. A ship has no such built-in motion, so שמואל says only pulling the whole ship counts. Now both sides of the suggested match are knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one, here meaning the other legs

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to tie רב and שמואל to the animal ברייתא fails: animals and ships move differently, so each אמורא can fit either תנא.

phrases.english: And Shmuel could say:
I said my ruling even according to the first Tanna.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
phrases.english: The first Tanna only said his rule
about animals,
because once it has lifted a front leg and a back leg,
the other legs are ready to be lifted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל סְפִינָה, אִי מָשֵׁיךְ לַהּ כּוּלַּהּ – אִין,
phrases.english: But a ship, if he pulls the whole of it, yes, he acquires it;
if not, he does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes rejecting the match by freeing שמואל from רבי אחא, just as step 24 freed רב.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that שמואל must disagree with the תנא קמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion ignored that an animal's first step leads naturally into walking, while a ship has no such natural motion.

steps.title: A second try: a ברייתא on acquiring a ship and 'letters' by pulling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a different ברייתא as the source of the רב/שמואל dispute: the תנא קמא says a ship is acquired by pulling, and רבי נתן says a ship and 'letters' are acquired by pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: a ship is acquired by pulling. רבי נתן says: a ship and letters are acquired by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new attempt to match רב and שמואל to תנאים, using a ברייתא that talks about a ship directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first ברייתא, this one is about ships themselves. The ברייתא continues on the next amud, where the גמרא explains how it connects to רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'letters'; the debt written in a loan document

phrases.english: Let us say this is like these Tannaim,
as it is taught: A ship is acquired by pulling.
Rabbi Natan says:
A ship and letters are acquired by pulling
phrases.notes: The 'letters' are a written loan document; you acquire the debt written in it by pulling the paper.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא כְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first match failed, the גמרא tries a different ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב and שמואל on pulling a ship.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the תנא קמא and רבי נתן discuss acquiring a ship (and 'letters') by pulling.
